title: Falcon Freight remittance update: look-alike domain and no portal request
scenario_text:
Falcon Freight's accounts payable team receives an email from a long-standing supplier, Cormorant Packaging, attaching a $92,300 invoice marked 'PAST DUE - please remit today to avoid a shipment hold.' The email says the supplier has switched banks and provides new account and routing numbers. The payment run closes in two hours.

In the #ap-processing Slack channel the AP clerk writes: 'Checked it out - invoice matches an open PO in NetSuite, amounts line up, and the contact name is the same rep we always deal with. Looks legit, I'm queuing it for today's payment run.'

Several other systems are worth reconciling before releasing funds. The email arrived from cormorant-packaging.co, whereas the domain on file in the vendor master, and the address every prior email from this vendor has used, is cormorant-packaging.com. In Coupa, the vendor's self-service portal shows no bank-change request was ever submitted - Coupa is the contractually required channel for updating remittance details. The new routing number belongs to a bank in a different state than the vendor's headquarters. The invoice number on the PDF, INV-55018, matches an invoice NetSuite shows was already paid in full six weeks ago.

The clerk's 'matches the PO' check is real, but here every corroborating control fails: the sender domain is a look-alike, the bank change never came through the verified portal, the routing geography is off, and the invoice was already paid. You are the AP supervisor reviewing the queue. Weighing the clerk's verification against the domain mismatch, the absent portal request, and the out-of-state routing details, what should you do with this $92,300 payment before the run closes?
question: What should AP do with the $92,300 payment before the payment run closes?
changed_fact: In the base, the bank-change email arrives from the vendor's verified domain of record and a matching bank-change request exists in the Coupa vendor portal; in the variant, the email arrives from a look-alike domain and no portal request was ever submitted.
choices: Pay the invoice to the new account immediately because of its urgency; the PO match in NetSuite alone confirms the request is legitimate.

Process the payment to the new bank account: the change was submitted through the vendor's verified Coupa portal and the sender domain matches the vendor's domain of record, so the remittance update is authenticated.
Hold the payment and verify the bank-account change out-of-band using a known vendor contact before releasing any funds.
Split the payment - send half now to meet the deadline and half after later verification - to preserve the vendor relationship.
